reviews.title: No UHD/4K
reviews.text: Very disappointed that the BBC iPlayer app on Apple TV 4K does not, and apparently never will, support UHD. The whole point of buying Apple TV 4K is to enjoy programmes in the best quality, yet iPlayer is stuck with a legacy version that doesn’t even offer full HD properly. Other devices and smart TVs get UHD, subtitles, and modern features, but Apple TV users are left behind. This feels neglected and out of date, and it doesn’t reflect the capabilities of the hardware or what viewers should reasonably expect in 2025.

reviews.title: Remember my continue watching lists

reviews.title: Problems
reviews.text:
We’re stuck with BBC iPlayer if we want to watch BBC programmes on iOS. Here’s an example of it’s stupidity:
I watched the most recent episode of Strictly, and at the end I got “Next episode” - what?! I tapped on it and it transpires that we’re supposed to watch everyone’s dances all over again, one after another; are you kidding me?!  

I want iPlayer to tell me when the next episode of Strictly is on! If the next episodes that I’m given are not actually “episodes” but “extras”, how am I supposed to get to the genuine “Next episode” and how am I to know when it’s ready to view? This is utter madness.

reviews.title: A-Z has disappeared
reviews.text: Why has the A-Z option in the film section been removed on my iPad? It was so much easier to find the film I wanted without having to trawl through a category I think it might possibly be in. Please bring it back!

reviews.title: Totalitarian Propaganda
reviews.text:
Sadly this app is of the same low standard I have come to expect of the BBC offerings more generally, including that of the news coverage I once trusted and respected but which has since precipitously declined. 

It pains me to watch a once great institution so quickly crumbling.

reviews.title: Killer Couple
reviews.text: I  think if you are going to review a programme,  you should present both sides and just because the woman was 100 miles away from the crime scene; doesn’t make her not guilty.  What would she suggest as an alternative punishment??? I’m guessing that she knew what was going to happen to the victim and there was no supporting evidence that she didn’t.  The  reporter was totally biased , to the extent that she was really, really annoying and demonstrated her total lack of journalistic skills, by turning this into a one dimensional crime.  She  didn’t focus on the criteria that convicted her and left you feeling that she was  her own personal cheerleader, with barely a thought for the victim’s relatives that are left dealing with this hideous and vicious crime.    Shocking example of journalism - naive, inept - pathetic and really, really annoying - listening to her banging on about the 100 away, so not guilty.  Just a terrible documentary  -
